observation: Host of FRB 121102 is a low-metallicity, low-mass dwarf star-forming galaxy at z=0.19273, resembling hosts of superluminous supernovae and long GRBs.
locator: abstract; host redshift and SED/metallicity section
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse
confidence_note: Localization and host association are secure; the SLSN/LGRB-host analogy is the authors' interpretation, not a measurement.
unresolved_ambiguity: One object. Later localizations show dwarf hosts are the minority, so this cannot be generalized to the population.

observation: Compact, luminous persistent radio source (PRS) spatially coincident with FRB 121102 to within the localization precision (sub-arcsecond, VLA; later milliarcsecond-scale with VLBI).
locator: abstract; VLA localization and persistent-source photometry
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse (young magnetar in dense nebula)
confidence_note: Existence and compactness of the PRS are robust; its physical nature is not established by the detection itself.
unresolved_ambiguity: PRS could be a magnetar wind nebula, a young supernova remnant, or an accretion-powered source (low-luminosity AGN / X-ray binary analogue). Degenerate.

observation: FRB 121102 bursts are coincident with a bright star-forming knot (HII region) within the dwarf host rather than with the host nucleus.
locator: abstract; HST/optical imaging of the star-forming region
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse
confidence_note: Association with the star-forming knot is strong; the precise offset in parsecs is not quoted here because I am not confident of the exact figure.
unresolved_ambiguity: Coincidence with a star-forming region does not by itself establish a young age; the star-forming knot dominates the host light, so chance alignment is not negligible.

observation: FRB 20190520B is a second repeater with a compact persistent radio source in a dwarf star-forming host, i.e. the 121102-like configuration is not unique.
locator: abstract; host identification and persistent-source sections
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse (young magnetar in dense nebula)
confidence_note: Detection secure. Whether the PRS is powered the same way as in FRB 121102 is assumed, not shown.
unresolved_ambiguity: Both PRS systems are repeaters with extreme dispersion and rotation measures; unclear whether this is a separate sub-class or an early evolutionary stage common to all sources.

observation: FRB 20180916B localized with milliarcsecond precision to a star-forming region in the outskirts of a nearby, massive spiral galaxy at z=0.0337.
locator: abstract; EVN localization and host identification
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse
confidence_note: Localization is secure. Support is weaker than for FRB 121102 because a normal spiral host is not a distinctive prediction of this channel.
unresolved_ambiguity: A massive spiral host is compatible with essentially every progenitor hypothesis; the host type alone carries little discriminating power.

observation: FRB 20180916B is offset by roughly a few hundred parsecs from the nearest bright star-forming knot, with no coincident young stellar population at the burst position.
citation: Tendulkar et al. 2021, ApJL (60 pc environment of FRB 20180916B)
locator: abstract; offset from nearest star-forming knot
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse with a very young (<~ few hundred year) magnetar
confidence_note: I am confident of the qualitative offset result but NOT of the exact parsec value; verify the number against the source before quoting it.
unresolved_ambiguity: Offset can be explained by a natal kick plus an age of >~1e5 yr, by a runaway progenitor, or by an older formation channel; these are not separated by the imaging.

observation: FRB 20200120E localized to a globular cluster associated with M81, i.e. to an old, metal-poor, low-star-formation stellar environment.
locator: abstract; VLBI localization and globular cluster identification
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse
confidence_note: Localization to the globular cluster is secure and the cluster's old age is well established from stellar populations.
unresolved_ambiguity: Rules out core collapse for THIS source only. Whether it represents a rare channel or a substantial fraction of the population is unknown.

observation: Same globular-cluster localization read as positive evidence for compact-object formation channels available to old populations (accretion-induced collapse of a white dwarf, WD-WD or NS-WD merger products, dynamically assembled binaries).
locator: abstract and discussion of formation channels
hypothesis: magnetar-alternative-channel (AIC / merger / dynamical assembly)
confidence_note: The environment strongly constrains the formation channel; the specific channel among AIC / merger / dynamical capture is not determined.
unresolved_ambiguity: Globular clusters have high stellar interaction rates, so per-star rates there are not transferable to field populations; the channel could be strongly over-represented in clusters.

observation: FRB 20200120E has a very low dispersion measure (~88 pc cm^-3 total), leaving little room for a dense magnetized local nebula along the line of sight.
locator: abstract; DM budget and M81 association
hypothesis: all FRB sources sit inside dense young nebulae (as inferred for FRB 121102)
confidence_note: DM value is well measured; the DM budget decomposition into Milky Way, halo, host and local contributions carries modelling uncertainty.
unresolved_ambiguity: A low integrated DM does not exclude a compact, low-filling-factor magnetized region very close to the source.

observation: Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154 emitted an FRB-like millisecond radio burst (fluence of order 1 MJy ms) simultaneously with a hard X-ray burst.
citation: CHIME/FRB Collaboration 2020, Nature; Bochenek et al. 2020, Nature
locator: abstracts; burst detection and fluence
hypothesis: magnetar (any formation channel) as an FRB engine
confidence_note: Detection by two independent instruments; magnetar identification unambiguous. Establishes existence, not dominance, of a magnetar channel.
unresolved_ambiguity: Shows magnetars CAN make FRB-like bursts; does not show that the cosmological FRB population is made this way.

observation: Isotropic-equivalent radio energy of the SGR 1935+2154 burst is ~1e34-3e35 erg (distance-dependent), roughly 4-5 orders of magnitude below a typical cosmological FRB and ~7 dex below the brightest localized events.
source_name: SGR 1935+2154 (Galactic magnetar); cosmological FRB comparison set
citation: artifact:frb_energetics_scaling.py and artifact:frb_energetics_scaling_out.txt - unit conversion of published fluences to isotropic energy
locator: frb_energetics_scaling_out.txt, ratio block
hypothesis: magnetars like SGR 1935+2154 as the sole engine of cosmological FRBs
confidence_note: Conversion is arithmetic, not a measurement; distance to SGR 1935+2154 is uncertain by ~factor 3 (about 1 dex in energy), and E_iso scales linearly with the assumed bandwidth.
unresolved_ambiguity: Unknown whether the energy gap is a continuous luminosity function extending over 7 dex or evidence for physically distinct populations; selection effects truncate the faint end.

observation: Bursts from FRB 20200120E in the M81 globular cluster have isotropic energies overlapping the Galactic magnetar burst range, bridging part of the Galactic/extragalactic energy gap.
citation: artifact:frb_energetics_scaling_out.txt - representative 1 Jy ms burst at 3.6 Mpc gives ~1.6e34 erg, below the 9 kpc SGR 1935+2154 value
locator: frb_energetics_scaling_out.txt, case table row 4
hypothesis: a single continuous FRB luminosity function spanning Galactic to cosmological energies
confidence_note: Uses a representative rather than a measured fluence for FRB 20200120E; treat as an order-of-magnitude framing only, not as a published energy.
unresolved_ambiguity: Overlap in energy does not imply a shared mechanism; a nearby low-energy repeater in an old cluster may belong to a different channel entirely.

observation: FRB host galaxies span a wide range of stellar masses and star formation rates and are typically ordinary star-forming galaxies, not the extreme low-mass, low-metallicity systems that dominate SLSN and long-GRB host samples.
citation: Bhandari et al. 2020, ApJL; Heintz et al. 2020, ApJ
locator: abstracts; host demographic comparison to transient host samples
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse specifically via the SLSN/LGRB formation channel
confidence_note: Conclusion rests on small samples (tens of hosts) with heterogeneous selection; statistical comparisons to transient host samples are sensitive to the comparison sample chosen.
unresolved_ambiguity: Whether FRB rate tracks stellar mass, star formation rate, or some mixture is unresolved; current samples cannot cleanly separate these.

observation: Expanded ASKAP-era host sample confirms a mix of star-forming and low-specific-star-formation hosts with moderate stellar masses; no single host type dominates.
source_name: localized FRB host sample (ASKAP/CRAFT and others)
locator: abstract; host property tables and comparison figures
hypothesis: a single young-progenitor channel producing all FRBs
confidence_note: Selection favours bright, low-redshift, well-imaged hosts; unbiased demographics are not yet available.
unresolved_ambiguity: Host diversity is consistent both with several progenitor channels and with one channel having a broad delay-time distribution.

observation: FRB 180924 localized to a massive galaxy with low specific star formation rate, offset several kiloparsecs from the galaxy centre; no star-forming knot at the burst position.
locator: abstract; host identification and offset measurement
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse with a young magnetar
confidence_note: Localization is secure; the inference of an old progenitor from the integrated host colours is model-dependent.
unresolved_ambiguity: Low-level, spatially localized star formation below the imaging limit cannot be excluded at the burst position.

observation: FRB 190523 localized to a massive galaxy with a low star formation rate, unlike the dwarf host of FRB 121102.
locator: abstract; host association and stellar population discussion
hypothesis: magnetar-core-collapse with a young magnetar
confidence_note: Localization region is larger than for VLBI-localized sources; host association is probabilistic rather than definitive.
unresolved_ambiguity: Single source; does not exclude a young magnetar formed in a low-luminosity star-forming pocket within the massive host.

observation: Projected host-centric offsets of localized FRBs, from HST imaging, mostly fall within the host stellar light at a few kiloparsecs, tracking the light distribution more closely than short-GRB offsets but less tightly than core-collapse SNe.
locator: abstract; offset distribution and comparison to transient classes
hypothesis: compact-object merger (NS-NS / NS-BH) as the dominant FRB channel
confidence_note: Small sample (order ten hosts) and projected (not physical) offsets; the comparison-class offset distributions themselves carry uncertainty.
unresolved_ambiguity: Intermediate offsets are also produced by kicked neutron stars from core collapse, so the offset distribution alone does not separate the channels.

observation: Persistent radio sources are rare: only two secure PRS associations (FRB 121102 and FRB 20190520B) among several tens of well-localized FRBs.
citation: Chatterjee et al. 2017, Nature; Niu et al. 2022, Nature
locator: abstracts of both, read together with the absence of comparable detections elsewhere
hypothesis: all FRB sources are embedded in luminous young magnetized nebulae
confidence_note: The non-detections are heterogeneous in depth and mostly not published as a uniform limit set; this row is a statement about the published record, not a rate measurement.
unresolved_ambiguity: PRS rarity may reflect source age (nebulae fade) rather than distinct progenitors. A uniform limit compilation is needed; see the open task frb-task-prs-incidence.

observation: FRB 20220610A localized to z=1.016, the most distant well-localized FRB at the time of publication, in a morphologically complex, apparently interacting galaxy system.
locator: abstract; redshift determination and host imaging
hypothesis: progenitors form in star-forming systems and exist out to z~1
confidence_note: Redshift is spectroscopic and secure; the interacting/compact-group interpretation of the host morphology is less certain.
unresolved_ambiguity: Whether the host is a single disturbed galaxy or a group affects host DM and stellar-mass estimates, and hence the inferred environment.

observation: Implied isotropic energy of FRB 20220610A is of order 1e42 erg under standard bandwidth assumptions, near the top of the observed FRB energy distribution.
citation: artifact:frb_energetics_scaling_out.txt - 45 Jy ms at z=1.016 gives 1.28e42 erg for a 1 GHz bandwidth
locator: frb_energetics_scaling_out.txt, case table final row
hypothesis: energetic ceiling of magnetar-powered emission models
confidence_note: The input fluence (45 Jy ms) is approximate and should be VERIFIED against Ryder et al. 2023; the energy scales linearly with the assumed bandwidth.
unresolved_ambiguity: Magnetar magnetic energy reservoirs plausibly reach 1e47-1e49 erg, so a 1e42 erg burst is not obviously prohibitive; the constraint bites only through the radio efficiency, which is unknown.

observation: Dispersion measures of localized FRBs follow the expected DM-redshift (Macquart) relation, confirming that most of the DM is intergalactic and accounting for the cosmic baryon content.
locator: abstract; DM-z relation fit
hypothesis: all progenitor hypotheses (consistency check, not a discriminant)
confidence_note: Result is robust for the sample used but rests on a small number of localizations and on an assumed cosmic baryon distribution model.
unresolved_ambiguity: Scatter in the relation absorbs host plus local DM contributions, so individual local-environment densities remain poorly constrained by this method.

observation: Host plus local DM contributions inferred from the Macquart relation are typically modest (order 100 pc cm^-3 or less in the rest frame) for most localized FRBs.
locator: abstract and DM budget discussion; inference by this contributor from the fit residuals
hypothesis: FRB sources generically sit in dense young supernova remnants or magnetar nebulae
confidence_note: This is a downstream inference by this contributor, not a stated result of the paper; the host DM inference is degenerate with the assumed IGM model and is weakened by small samples.
unresolved_ambiguity: A young dense remnant contributes strongly to DM for only a few hundred years, so a modest host DM may indicate age rather than a different progenitor.

observation: CHIME/FRB Catalog 1 reports 536 FRBs including 62 bursts from 18 repeating sources, and an inferred sky rate of roughly 800 events per sky per day above about 5 Jy ms at 400-800 MHz.
locator: abstract; population and rate sections
hypothesis: cataclysmic one-off channels (compact-object mergers) as the dominant FRB source
confidence_note: The sky rate is well measured for CHIME's band and selection function; converting it to a volumetric rate for comparison with merger rates requires an assumed luminosity function and redshift distribution.
unresolved_ambiguity: The rate argument can be evaded by strong beaming or by a luminosity function with many faint events; it constrains but does not exclude cataclysmic channels.

observation: The observed repeater fraction in CHIME/FRB Catalog 1 is small (order a few percent of sources) but is consistent with a scenario in which all sources repeat at low rates, given the finite exposure.
locator: abstract; repeater statistics section
hypothesis: all FRBs repeat (single population)
confidence_note: Exposure-limited. The measured fraction is a lower limit on the true repeating fraction, not an estimate of it.
unresolved_ambiguity: Fundamental degeneracy between a broad repetition-rate distribution in one population and two genuinely distinct populations; see frb-open-question-all-repeat.

observation: Bursts from repeaters are on average temporally broader and spectrally narrower (more band-limited) than bursts from apparent non-repeaters in the CHIME sample.
locator: abstract; morphological classification and comparison of the two samples
hypothesis: all FRBs repeat (single population with identical emission physics)
confidence_note: The morphological difference is statistically significant in the CHIME sample but is sensitive to instrumental selection on bandwidth and duration.
unresolved_ambiguity: A morphological difference can arise from viewing geometry, beaming, or propagation within a single population; it does not by itself require two progenitor classes.
